name: Ferrous Fumarate
contraindications: Known iron overload states (e.g., haemochromatosis), anaemia of other specified causes unless iron deficiency demonstrated, known hypersensitivity
interactions: Absorption reduced by antacids, calcium, and some antibiotics (quinolones, tetracyclines); separate dosing where possible; vitamin C can enhance absorption
monitoring: Monitor hemoglobin, mean cell volume and reticulocyte response; check ferritin/iron studies to confirm response and guide duration of therapy
pregnancy: Generally safe and commonly used in pregnancy for iron deficiency under supervision
sideEffects: Gastrointestinal upset (nausea, abdominal pain), constipation or diarrhoea, dark stools; some formulations may be better tolerated
clinicalPearls: Choose formulation based on elemental iron content and tolerance; advise patient about dark stools and constipation, and give guidance on administration with regard to food and interacting medications
indication: Treatment and prevention of iron deficiency anaemia
